facts.text: San Felipe, founded in 1824 as San Felipe de Austin, was the first capital of Stephen F. Austin’s colony and the birthplace of the Texas Rangers.
The town’s main commercial street, Calle Commercio, was laid out by 1828, making San Felipe a bustling hub second only to San Antonio at the time.
In 1836, San Felipe was deliberately burned to prevent Mexican forces from capturing it, then rebuilt a few years later but never regained its former prominence.
The original townsite was donated to the state in 1940 and now serves as the San Felipe de Austin State Historic Site, preserving the colony’s legacy.
During the late nineteenth century, German settlers arrived in San Felipe, followed by Czechs, adding to the town’s diverse cultural tapestry.
San Felipe sits on the west bank of the Brazos River at 29°47′40″N 96°6′17″W, a location that once hosted Texas’s first post office and newspaper office.
